projects.name: Autonomous Trading Desk
projects.blurb: A multi-agent trading desk — a hedge fund in a box. Research agents surface theses from the news and price action, a quant agent prices and backtests them, a risk agent vetoes anything that breaches position or drawdown limits, and an execution agent works the resulting orders — all supervised by a human and every decision logged for the post-mortem.
projects.body:
A multi-agent trading desk — a hedge fund in a box. Research agents surface
theses from the news and price action, a quant agent prices and backtests them,
a risk agent vetoes anything that breaches position or drawdown limits, and an
execution agent works the resulting orders — all supervised by a human and every
decision logged for the post-mortem.

Structurally this is the same problem as coordinating a rescue fleet: many
autonomous actors sharing one picture, disagreeing, and being reconciled under
hard constraints — here the constraint is risk and capital instead of fuel and
comms. Market data feeds the picture through Polygon, gs-quant handles the
pricing and risk analytics, a dedicated library builds the portfolio, and orders
reach the market through the broker gateway. A local model runs the agent loop so
no thesis or position leaves the desk.

projects.name: Counter-UAS Engagement Simulator
projects.blurb: A Monte Carlo study tool for sizing a layered small-drone defense around a fixed site. Planners place radars, electro-optical/infrared cameras, and RF detectors on terrain, set an incoming threat mix — single drones, coordinated swarms, low-and-slow quadcopters hugging the tree line — and run thousands of raids. The output is how often each threat is detected, tracked, and handed off inside the time available. It is a sizing and placement tool, not a fire-control system.
projects.body:
A Monte Carlo study tool for sizing a layered small-drone defense around a
fixed site. Planners place radars, electro-optical/infrared cameras, and RF
detectors on terrain, set an incoming threat mix — single drones, coordinated
swarms, low-and-slow quadcopters hugging the tree line — and run thousands of
raids. The output is how often each threat is detected, tracked, and handed off
inside the time available. It is a sizing and placement tool, not a fire-control
system.

The value is in the coupled models. Sensor line-of-sight and coverage come from
an orbital and terrain analysis tool, radar cross-sections and antenna patterns
from electromagnetic simulation, and the attacking swarm is an agent-based model
whose behaviors — saturate, decoy, split up — are trained in a multi-agent
reinforcement-learning environment. Sweeps run in containers across a cluster.
It reuses the mission-rehearsal simulator's machinery with the roles reversed:
instead of flying the drones, you are trying to see them.

projects.name: Cyber Range Log Analyst
projects.blurb: An analyst's assistant for defensive cyber exercises on a training range. During the exercise it ingests network flows, host logs, and IDS alerts from the range and groups related alerts into incidents — this phishing click, that lateral movement, the later data staging. It writes a running timeline of each incident so the blue team can see the attack as a story rather than a thousand alerts, and the white cell can score their detection and response times.
projects.body:
An analyst's assistant for defensive cyber exercises on a training range.
During the exercise it ingests network flows, host logs, and IDS alerts from
the range and groups related alerts into incidents — this phishing click, that
lateral movement, the later data staging. It writes a running timeline of each
incident so the blue team can see the attack as a story rather than a thousand
alerts, and the white cell can score their detection and response times.

Logs, metrics, and traces land in a single observability store, so the
assistant queries one place rather than a dozen consoles. Single sign-on gives
the blue team, white cell, and observers separate views of the same data. A
local model clusters alerts, summarizes each incident with links to the
underlying log lines, and drafts the after-action report — keeping exercise
data, which often mirrors real network layouts, off any external service. It
uses the same observability stack as the RF spectrum network and points at the
homelab LLM gateway for its model.

projects.name: Technical-Document Intelligence Engine
projects.blurb: An engine that turns a wall of scanned specifications, drawings, and PDFs into a queryable knowledge base. It runs OCR over the scans, recovers document structure and tables, and builds a knowledge graph you can ask engineering questions against — with every answer citing the exact source document and page it came from.
projects.body:
An engine that turns a wall of scanned specifications, drawings, and PDFs into a
queryable knowledge base. It runs OCR over the scans, recovers document structure
and tables, and builds a knowledge graph you can ask engineering questions
against — with every answer citing the exact source document and page it came
from.

The hard part is trust: turning messy, unstructured, often hand-marked documents
into a grounded knowledge base an engineer will actually rely on. OCR and layout
recovery lift text and tables off the page, a document parser reconstructs the
logical structure, and a graph-backed retrieval layer stores the relationships so
retrieval is grounded rather than a bag of chunks. A local model does the reading
and answering, keeping proprietary documents on-premises. It is the same
"structure the chaos" theme as parsing radio traffic in the rescue fleet, aimed
at a filing cabinet instead of a radio net.

projects.name: Equity Factor Research Lab
projects.blurb: A research harness for cross-sectional equity factors — value, momentum, quality, low volatility, and a handful of ML-learned alphas — that measures each factor's information coefficient, turnover, and decay across holding periods before anything is allowed near a portfolio.
projects.body:
A research harness for cross-sectional equity factors — value, momentum,
quality, low volatility, and a handful of ML-learned alphas — that measures
each factor's information coefficient, turnover, and decay across holding
periods before anything is allowed near a portfolio.

The discipline is in the evaluation: point-in-time data so nothing leaks from
the future, factor returns neutralized against sector and size, regression
diagnostics on every exposure, and a tear sheet that shows drawdowns and
rolling Sharpe rather than one flattering number. Paused until the data
pipeline can serve survivorship-free fundamentals; the surviving factors are
meant to feed the portfolio optimizer as expected-return views.

projects.name: Field-Notes Transcriber
projects.blurb: Turns voice memos, meeting recordings, and site-walk dictation into searchable, speaker-labelled notes. Drop an audio file in a folder and it is transcribed, diarized, timestamped, summarized into action items, and indexed so you can ask "what did we decide about the antenna mount?" and land on the exact second of the recording.
projects.body:
Turns voice memos, meeting recordings, and site-walk dictation into searchable,
speaker-labelled notes. Drop an audio file in a folder and it is transcribed,
diarized, timestamped, summarized into action items, and indexed so you can ask
"what did we decide about the antenna mount?" and land on the exact second of
the recording.

Everything runs locally: a fast speech-to-text engine does the first pass, a
word-level alignment and diarization step attributes each sentence to a
speaker, and a local model writes the summary and answers questions over the
transcript archive through a chat front-end. Shipped and in daily use — it is
the audio sibling of the document intelligence engine, grounding answers in a
recording instead of a scanned page.

projects.name: Forward Additive Spares Depot
projects.blurb: A workflow for printing replacement parts at a forward location instead of waiting weeks for the supply chain. A maintainer identifies a failed part; the tool finds its technical data package, checks whether it is approved for additive manufacture and whether the material and printer on hand can meet its strength and temperature requirements, then prepares the print and records a qualification log tying the printed part to its source drawing, print settings, and inspection results.
projects.body:
A workflow for printing replacement parts at a forward location instead of
waiting weeks for the supply chain. A maintainer identifies a failed part; the
tool finds its technical data package, checks whether it is approved for
additive manufacture and whether the material and printer on hand can meet its
strength and temperature requirements, then prepares the print and records a
qualification log tying the printed part to its source drawing, print settings,
and inspection results.

The hard part is trust in the part. Technical data packages are often scanned
drawings and PDFs, so a document parser pulls dimensions, materials, and
tolerances out of them. Parametric CAD adapts the geometry when a printable
substitute needs thicker walls or a different orientation, and the slicer
produces the print with settings fixed per part. The readiness predictor tells
the depot which parts to stock material for; the fixture designer shares the
CAD and slicing pipeline.

projects.name: Generative Fixture Designer
projects.blurb: An idea for designing workholding fixtures automatically. Give it a part model and the machining operations planned for it, and it proposes soft jaws, vise fixtures, or a printed nest that locates the part repeatably, clears every tool path, and resists the cutting forces — then exports a printable or machinable fixture body.
projects.body:
An idea for designing workholding fixtures automatically. Give it a part model
and the machining operations planned for it, and it proposes soft jaws, vise
fixtures, or a printed nest that locates the part repeatably, clears every tool
path, and resists the cutting forces — then exports a printable or machinable
fixture body.

The interesting problem is reasoning about geometry under constraints: picking
datum faces, checking tool-path clearance, and trading print time against
stiffness. Parametric CAD scripts generate candidate fixtures, a slicer
estimates print time and material for the printed variants, and a local model
reads the setup sheet to infer which faces matter. It borrows the trade-space
sweep idea from the microgrid sizing study, aimed at a vise instead of a
battery bank.

projects.name: GSD Core App
projects.blurb: A local-first "get stuff done" runner that turns a plain-language goal into a sequence of executed steps. It plans a task graph, routes each step to a local model, and keeps the whole loop on the machine so nothing leaves the laptop.
projects.body:
A local-first "get stuff done" runner that turns a plain-language goal into a
sequence of executed steps. It plans a task graph, routes each step to a local
model, and keeps the whole loop on the machine so nothing leaves the laptop.

The core is a small library that other tools build on: a scheduler, a tool
registry, and a persistence layer for run history. Day-to-day development leans
on an AI editor for the glue code and a local model server for the planning and
reflection calls, so the whole thing runs without an API key.

projects.name: Homelab LLM Gateway
projects.blurb: A single, authenticated front door to every model running at home. It serves large models on the GPU box and small quantized ones on CPU nodes, exposes them behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint with per-user keys and quotas, and gives the household a shared chat interface with conversation history and document upload.
projects.body:
A single, authenticated front door to every model running at home. It serves
large models on the GPU box and small quantized ones on CPU nodes, exposes them
behind one OpenAI-compatible endpoint with per-user keys and quotas, and gives
the household a shared chat interface with conversation history and document
upload.

The interesting work is operational: routing each request to the cheapest
model that can handle it, batching to keep the GPU saturated, single sign-on
in front of everything, and tracing every call so latency, token spend, and
errors are visible. Containers on a small cluster keep it reproducible. The
other local-first projects — the transcriber, the copilot, the trading desk's
agents — all point at this gateway instead of each running their own model.

projects.name: MBSE Model Copilot
projects.blurb: An assistant that sits beside a systems model and keeps it honest. It reads requirement documents and interface control documents, proposes SysML v2 requirement definitions and satisfy links, flags requirements nothing satisfies, and answers questions like "which parts are affected if the uplink budget drops by 3 dB?" by walking the model rather than guessing.
projects.body:
An assistant that sits beside a systems model and keeps it honest. It reads
requirement documents and interface control documents, proposes SysML v2
requirement definitions and satisfy links, flags requirements nothing
satisfies, and answers questions like "which parts are affected if the uplink
budget drops by 3 dB?" by walking the model rather than guessing.

Two halves make it work: a document parser turns specifications into
structured text with tables intact, and a model-aware agent queries and edits
the textual SysML through an open-source modeling server while staying
round-trip compatible with the commercial tool the team already uses. A local
model keeps controlled technical data on-premises. The SAR fleet model is the
first test case — its requirements-trace gaps are exactly what the copilot
should close.

projects.name: Microgrid Dispatch & Resilience Optimizer
projects.blurb: A dispatch optimizer for a campus microgrid — solar, battery storage, a diesel backup, and a mix of controllable loads. It forecasts demand and generation for the day ahead, then schedules storage and generation to ride through grid outages at least cost, re-planning as the weather and the load actually unfold.
projects.body:
A dispatch optimizer for a campus microgrid — solar, battery storage, a diesel
backup, and a mix of controllable loads. It forecasts demand and generation for
the day ahead, then schedules storage and generation to ride through grid
outages at least cost, re-planning as the weather and the load actually unfold.

The complexity is closing the loop between a continuous physical model and a
discrete scheduling problem. The plant is modeled in Modelica so the physics of
batteries and inverters are honest, a ModelCenter study sweeps the sizing and
dispatch trade space, and an agent-based model of prosumers reacting to price
signals stresses the schedule against selfish behavior. A forecasting model
drives the day-ahead plan, and operators watch state of charge and reserve margin
on a live dashboard.

projects.name: Model Drift Monitor
projects.blurb: A monitoring service that watches deployed models for data drift and quietly degrading accuracy. It compares each day's feature distributions against the training reference, tracks prediction drift and delayed ground-truth accuracy, and opens an alert — with the offending features ranked — before a stale model does real damage.
projects.body:
A monitoring service that watches deployed models for data drift and quietly
degrading accuracy. It compares each day's feature distributions against the
training reference, tracks prediction drift and delayed ground-truth accuracy,
and opens an alert — with the offending features ranked — before a stale model
does real damage.

Reference datasets and model versions are pinned with data version control so
every alert points at the exact snapshot the model was trained on, statistical
drift reports are generated per feature, and the metrics and logs stream into
dashboards next to the rest of the infrastructure. The forecaster and the
sensor-anomaly detector are its first two customers; both suffer the same
distribution shift over time.

projects.name: Unusual Options-Flow Scanner
projects.blurb: A scanner that watches the live options tape for unusual activity — block prints well above open interest, sweeps hitting the ask across several exchanges, and sudden jumps in implied volatility on a single strike — and ranks each alert by how far it sits outside that contract's normal behavior.
projects.body:
A scanner that watches the live options tape for unusual activity — block
prints well above open interest, sweeps hitting the ask across several
exchanges, and sudden jumps in implied volatility on a single strike — and
ranks each alert by how far it sits outside that contract's normal behavior.

Every trade is enriched with greeks and implied volatility computed on the fly,
so an alert carries delta-adjusted notional rather than raw premium. Historical
quotes and trades come from a tick-level options feed, underlying prices from a
second market-data source, and a research terminal is used to sanity-check a
flagged name before it ever reaches the desk. Alert rates, latency, and feed
gaps are charted on a live dashboard. It is the natural input for the
vol-surface lab and the research agents on the trading desk.

projects.name: Options Vol-Surface Lab
projects.blurb: An idea, no code yet. I want to build and calibrate an implied-volatility surface for equity options: pull an options chain, fit a no-arbitrage surface across strikes and expiries, and price exotic payoffs off it. The interesting part is the calibration — SVI or SABR fits, arbitrage checks, and a clean way to interpolate the surface for pricing.
projects.body:
An idea, no code yet. I want to build and calibrate an implied-volatility
surface for equity options: pull an options chain, fit a no-arbitrage surface
across strikes and expiries, and price exotic payoffs off it. The interesting
part is the calibration — SVI or SABR fits, arbitrage checks, and a clean way to
interpolate the surface for pricing.

Because there is no declared stack, the recommendations below are the whole
suggested tech stack, inferred purely from this description — option pricing
libraries, a quant analytics toolkit, and a market-data feed for the chains.

projects.name: Practice-Room Coach
projects.blurb: A practice companion for piano that listens while you play, follows along in the score, and afterwards shows where tempo drifted, which passages had wrong or missed notes, and how a piece improved across a week of sessions. Spoken commands — "loop bars twelve to sixteen", "slow it to eighty percent" — keep your hands on the keys.
projects.body:
A practice companion for piano that listens while you play, follows along in
the score, and afterwards shows where tempo drifted, which passages had wrong
or missed notes, and how a piece improved across a week of sessions. Spoken
commands — "loop bars twelve to sixteen", "slow it to eighty percent" — keep
your hands on the keys.

On-device audio inference handles pitch and onset detection, a small
speech-recognition model listens for the voice commands, and a sight-reading
app supplies the scores and drills. Archived after the prototype: score
following on polyphonic audio needed more than a hobby budget, though the
onset-detection code was reused in the field-notes transcriber.

projects.name: Portfolio Optimizer
projects.blurb: A backtesting harness for portfolio construction. It takes a universe of tickers and a set of constraints, then compares allocation methods — mean variance, hierarchical risk parity, and a few risk-budgeting schemes — on the same out-of-sample window so the tradeoffs are visible side by side.
projects.body:
A backtesting harness for portfolio construction. It takes a universe of
tickers and a set of constraints, then compares allocation methods — mean
variance, hierarchical risk parity, and a few risk-budgeting schemes — on the
same out-of-sample window so the tradeoffs are visible side by side.

Uses a dedicated optimization library for the allocation math and gs-quant for
the risk and pricing pieces. Paused while I decide whether to add a proper
market-data source instead of the CSVs it reads today.

projects.name: RF Spectrum Situational Awareness
projects.blurb: A distributed spectrum-monitoring network built from small passive software-defined-radio sensors. Each node sweeps its band, classifies the emitters it hears, and flags interference or jamming. The nodes share what they see over a peer-to-peer mesh, building one picture of a contested spectrum that the comms planner can use to switch frequency or route before a link actually drops.
projects.body:
A distributed spectrum-monitoring network built from small passive
software-defined-radio sensors. Each node sweeps its band, classifies the
emitters it hears, and flags interference or jamming. The nodes share what
they see over a peer-to-peer mesh, building one picture of a contested
spectrum that the comms planner can use to switch frequency or route before a
link actually drops.

The hard part is classification at the edge with intermittent backhaul. An RF
framework handles signal detection, demodulation, and fingerprinting on each
node. The mesh layer syncs detections opportunistically when neighbors are in
range, and a local model turns raw detections into plain-language reports for
the operator ("wideband noise on the UHF relay band, onset 14:02, bearing
north-east"). Detection rates, false alarms, and sensor health stream into
observability dashboards, and the classifier is watched for drift as the RF
environment changes. It is the sensing half of the contested-comms SAR mesh:
that project survives a jammed link, this one sees the jamming coming.

projects.name: Sales Account Researcher
projects.blurb: An agent that prepares a one-page brief before every sales call. Given a company name, it browses the company's site, recent filings, press releases, and job postings, extracts who the buyers are, what they are hiring for, and which initiatives were just announced, and drafts three tailored talking points with a citation behind every claim.
projects.body:
An agent that prepares a one-page brief before every sales call. Given a
company name, it browses the company's site, recent filings, press releases,
and job postings, extracts who the buyers are, what they are hiring for, and
which initiatives were just announced, and drafts three tailored talking points
with a citation behind every claim.

The research loop is a tool-using agent driving a headless browser, a
knowledge-base layer stores what it learns so the next brief on the same
account starts warm, and a workflow-automation tool kicks off a brief whenever
a meeting lands on the calendar and files the result into the CRM. It shares
the "answer only with a source" rule of the document intelligence engine,
pointed at the open web instead of a filing cabinet.

projects.name: Contested-Comms SAR Mesh
projects.blurb: The same rescue fleet, but assuming the radios drop. This project layers a resilient communications mesh over the SAR fleet so vessels and drones keep sharing a common operating picture when the link to shore is jammed, over the horizon, or saturated. Craft relay for each other, buffer telemetry through outages, and fall back to intermittent satellite passes — and the task allocator has to keep planning while it only sometimes knows where everyone is.
projects.body:
The same rescue fleet, but assuming the radios drop. This project layers a
resilient communications mesh over the SAR fleet so vessels and drones keep
sharing a common operating picture when the link to shore is jammed, over the
horizon, or saturated. Craft relay for each other, buffer telemetry through
outages, and fall back to intermittent satellite passes — and the task allocator
has to keep planning while it only sometimes knows where everyone is.

This one is genuinely multi-disciplinary. Antenna patterns and link budgets are
modeled in HFSS and CST, satellite relay windows and line-of-sight come from STK,
the peer-to-peer sync layer is built on iroh, and a UAF architecture ties the
operational, system, and resource views together so the comms design traces back
to the mission. The open research question is decentralized task allocation under
partial observability: agents that commit to a search plan, degrade gracefully as
neighbors go dark, and reconcile the picture when the mesh heals.

projects.name: SAR Fleet Coordinator
projects.blurb: Coordination software for search-and-rescue missions flown by a mixed fleet of unmanned surface vessels and UAVs. An incident commander drops a last-known position and a drift model; the planner divides the search area into cells, assigns each craft a sweep pattern sized to its sensor footprint and endurance, and re-tasks the fleet live as the probability-of-detection map updates from every pass.
projects.body:
Coordination software for search-and-rescue missions flown by a mixed fleet of
unmanned surface vessels and UAVs. An incident commander drops a last-known
position and a drift model; the planner divides the search area into cells,
assigns each craft a sweep pattern sized to its sensor footprint and endurance,
and re-tasks the fleet live as the probability-of-detection map updates from
every pass.

The hard part is the joint plan: many craft, overlapping sensor coverage, comms
and fuel limits, and a survivor whose position drifts with wind and current. A
multi-agent policy handles the task allocation, STK supplies the sensor- and
comms-coverage geometry, and the whole system-of-systems — vehicle, payload, and
ground-station interfaces — is specified in SysML so the pieces stay consistent
as the fleet grows. An on-board local model turns messy radio traffic into
structured tasking, and the ground station watches fleet health on a live
dashboard.

requirements.name: SearchCoverage

requirements.name: EnduranceMargin
requirements.text: Each assigned sweep shall leave >= 20% fuel/battery reserve for RTB.

requirements.name: DegradedComms
requirements.text: Craft shall continue the last valid tasking for 10 min on loss of link.

projects.name: Satellite Collection Planner
projects.blurb: A scheduler for a small Earth-observation constellation. Analysts submit collection requests — image this port daily, revisit this region within six hours of a cue, record emitters in this area — and the planner assigns each request to a satellite pass. It balances priority, cloud forecasts, sensor slew limits, onboard storage, and ground-station downlink windows, and re-plans the whole schedule when an urgent request arrives.
projects.body:
A scheduler for a small Earth-observation constellation. Analysts submit
collection requests — image this port daily, revisit this region within six
hours of a cue, record emitters in this area — and the planner assigns each
request to a satellite pass. It balances priority, cloud forecasts, sensor
slew limits, onboard storage, and ground-station downlink windows, and re-plans
the whole schedule when an urgent request arrives.

Access windows, sensor footprints, and downlink contacts come from orbital
analysis, so the planner only ever reasons about geometry that is physically
possible. Allocation is treated as a multi-agent problem: each satellite bids
on requests it can serve, and a policy trained in a multi-agent
reinforcement-learning environment learns when to hold capacity back for
cue-driven requests rather than filling every pass. Request backlog, fulfilment
rate, and age-of-information per target sit on a live dashboard. It is the
orbital cousin of the SAR fleet coordinator's re-tasking problem, and the
satellite relay windows it computes are the same ones the contested-comms mesh
falls back on.

projects.name: Sensor Telemetry Anomalies
projects.blurb: An idea for detecting anomalies in industrial sensor streams over time. The plan: ingest telemetry from many sensors, resample the irregular timestamps onto a regular grid, decompose trend and seasonality, and fit a rolling forecast so points that break the predicted band get flagged.
projects.body:
An idea for detecting anomalies in industrial sensor streams over time. The
plan: ingest telemetry from many sensors, resample the irregular timestamps
onto a regular grid, decompose trend and seasonality, and fit a rolling forecast
so points that break the predicted band get flagged.

Structurally this is the same shape as forecasting a financial series — lagged
features, rolling windows, drift as the distribution shifts over time, and a
signal that fires when the observed value leaves the forecast window. Different
domain, same temporal machinery, so the tooling should overlap heavily.

projects.name: Sustainment & Readiness Predictor
projects.blurb: Predictive maintenance for a vehicle fleet. It combines maintenance-action records, onboard sensor telemetry, and parts-supply data to forecast which components on which vehicles are likely to fail in the next 30, 60, and 90 days. It then recommends which spares to order and which inspections to pull forward so that mission readiness does not drop.
projects.body:
Predictive maintenance for a vehicle fleet. It combines maintenance-action
records, onboard sensor telemetry, and parts-supply data to forecast which
components on which vehicles are likely to fail in the next 30, 60, and 90 days.
It then recommends which spares to order and which inspections to pull forward
so that mission readiness does not drop.

Half the problem is the data. Decades of maintenance history live in scanned
work orders and technical manuals, so OCR and document parsing lift fault codes,
parts, and procedures off the page into structured records. A survival-style
failure model trains on the cleaned history, with every training snapshot
version-controlled so a prediction can be traced back to the data behind it.
Drift reports catch a model going stale when a new vehicle variant or operating
theater changes the failure patterns. A local model explains each
recommendation and cites the manual paragraph and maintenance records behind
it. It reuses the sensor-anomaly detector's temporal machinery and the document
engine's OCR pipeline.

projects.name: Tactical Radio-to-Report
projects.blurb: Turns push-to-talk radio traffic into structured reports, entirely on a rugged laptop or handheld with no connection to anything. It listens to a net, transcribes each transmission through static, clipping, and callsign jargon, and fills the right template — a 9-line medevac request, a situation report, a spot report — highlighting any required line that is missing so the operator can ask for it before the sender goes off the air.
projects.body:
Turns push-to-talk radio traffic into structured reports, entirely on a
rugged laptop or handheld with no connection to anything. It listens to a net,
transcribes each transmission through static, clipping, and callsign jargon, and
fills the right template — a 9-line medevac request, a situation report, a
spot report — highlighting any required line that is missing so the operator
can ask for it before the sender goes off the air.

The hard parts are the audio and the format. Radio audio is narrowband, noisy,
and full of procedure words and phonetic-alphabet grid references, so a small
speech-to-text model is tuned on that vocabulary and a faster batch pass
re-transcribes recordings afterwards for the log. A local model maps the
transcript onto the report fields and normalizes grids, times, and callsigns.
It is the field-notes transcriber hardened for a radio net, and the same
"messy radio traffic into structured tasking" step the SAR fleet coordinator
needs from its incident net.

projects.name: Trading Time-Series Forecaster
projects.blurb: Walk-forward forecasting of equity price series. It builds lagged features and rolling-window statistics from the raw series, trains a model per volatility regime, and validates strictly out-of-sample so nothing leaks from the future.
projects.body:
Walk-forward forecasting of equity price series. It builds lagged features and
rolling-window statistics from the raw series, trains a model per volatility
regime, and validates strictly out-of-sample so nothing leaks from the future.

The interesting problems are all temporal: resampling to a regular grid,
handling gaps and irregular timestamps, decomposing trend and seasonality, and
measuring drift as the distribution shifts over time. The output is a forecast
band and a signal that fires when the observed value breaks the predicted
window.

projects.name: UAS Mission Rehearsal Simulator
projects.blurb: A simulator for rehearsing multi-drone missions before they fly. Planners load terrain, airspace restrictions, weather, and a fleet roster, then run hundreds of Monte Carlo rehearsals in which vehicles lose links, batteries sag in the cold, and targets move — producing a mission-success distribution instead of a single optimistic plan.
projects.body:
A simulator for rehearsing multi-drone missions before they fly. Planners load
terrain, airspace restrictions, weather, and a fleet roster, then run hundreds
of Monte Carlo rehearsals in which vehicles lose links, batteries sag in the
cold, and targets move — producing a mission-success distribution instead of a
single optimistic plan.

Sensor footprints and line-of-sight geometry come from an orbital and terrain
analysis tool, an agent-based model plays the environment and the other
airspace users, and a multi-agent reinforcement-learning environment lets the
same allocation policy used by the SAR fleet coordinator be trained and stress
tested here first. Runs are containerized so a sweep fans out across a
cluster, and the outcome distributions land on a dashboard.
